context.doc: Context overrides the parent LookupConfig context for this mapping. Valid values: "record", "resource". Default: inherits from parent LookupConfig.

default.doc: Default is the value to use when the lookup returns no result. If not set and the lookup fails, no attribute is written. Optional.

destination.doc: Destination is the attribute key to write the result to. Required.

source.doc: Source is the field name in the lookup result for map results. Leave empty for 1:1 scalar lookups. Optional.

item.doc: AttributeMapping defines where to write a lookup result.

attributes.doc: Attributes defines where to write lookup results. Required: at least one mapping.

context.doc: Context is the default context for destination attributes. Valid values: "record", "resource". Default: "record"

key.doc: Key is an OTTL value expression for extracting the lookup key. Examples: attributes["user.id"], Trim(attributes["raw.id"]), resource.attributes["service.name"] Required.

item.doc: LookupConfig defines a single lookup rule.

lookups.doc: Lookups defines the lookup rules. Each rule specifies a key expression to extract the lookup value, and one or more attribute mappings for where to write the results.

Config.doc: Config holds the source-specific configuration as raw map. It is decoded into the source's typed config struct by the factory at processor creation time.

type.doc: Type is the source type identifier (e.g., "noop", "yaml").

source.doc: SourceConfig captures the source type and its opaque settings. Source-specific fields are collected into Config via mapstructure's ",remain" tag and decoded later in the factory's createSource using a mapstructure decoder. An alternative would be to implement confmap.Unmarshaler on Config (like geoipprocessor does) to resolve the source config at unmarshal time. We defer decoding to the factory because the set of available source factories is not known until the factory is constructed (custom sources can be injected via WithSources), so the config layer cannot look up the correct factory. Both paths run during collector startup, so validation timing is equivalent in practice.

limit_mib.doc: hard limit in MiB; above it the processor starts refusing data

limit_percentage.doc: hard limit as a percentage of total memory, for containers

spike_limit_mib.doc: headroom in MiB reserved for allocation spikes

spike_limit_percentage.doc: spike headroom as a percentage of total memory

scale_by.doc: A constant number by which the first operand will be scaled. A required field if the type is scale.

unit.doc: Unit for the new metric being generated.

rules.doc: Set of rules for generating new metrics

experimental_scale.doc: Scale is a scalar to multiply the values with.

label.doc: Label identifies the exact label to operate on.

label_set.doc: LabelSet is a list of labels to keep. All other labels are aggregated based on the AggregationType.

label_value.doc: LabelValue identifies the exact label value to operate on

new_label.doc: NewLabel determines the name to rename the identified label to.

new_value.doc: NewValue is used to set a new label value either when the operation is `AggregatedValues` or `addLabel`.
NewValue specifies the label value to rename to.

value.doc: Value specifies the current label value.

value_actions.doc: ValueActions is a list of renaming actions for label values.

operations.doc: Operations contains a list of operations that will be performed on the resulting metric(s).

submatch_case.doc: SubmatchCase specifies what case to use for label values created from regexp submatches.

transforms.doc: transform specifies a list of transforms on metrics with each transform focusing on one metric.

fields.doc: Config defines configuration for Resource processor.

fail_closed.doc: FailClosed indicates to not sample data (the processor will fail "closed") in case of error, such as failure to parse the tracestate field or missing the randomness attribute. By default, failure cases are sampled (the processor is fails "open").  Sampling priority-based decisions are made after FailClosed is processed, making it possible to sample despite errors using priority.

from_attribute.doc: FromAttribute (logs only) The optional name of a log record attribute used for sampling purposes, such as a unique log record ID. The value of the attribute is only used if the trace ID is absent or if `attribute_source` is set to `record`.

hash_seed.doc: HashSeed allows one to configure the hashing seed. This is important in scenarios where multiple layers of collectors have different sampling rates: if they use the same seed all passing one layer may pass the other even if they have different sampling rates, configuring different seeds avoids that.

mode.doc: Mode selects the sampling behavior. Supported values: - "hash_seed": the legacy behavior of this processor. Using an FNV hash combined with the HashSeed value, this sampler performs a non-consistent probabilistic downsampling.  The number of spans output is expected to equal SamplingPercentage (as a ratio) times the number of spans inpout, assuming good behavior from FNV and good entropy in the hashed attributes or TraceID. - "equalizing": Using an OTel-specified consistent sampling mechanism, this sampler selectively reduces the effective sampling probability of arriving spans.  This can be useful to select a small fraction of complete traces from a stream with mixed sampling rates.  The rate of spans passing through depends on how much sampling has already been applied.  If an arriving span was head sampled at the same probability it passes through.  If the span arrives with lower probability, a warning is logged because it means this sampler is configured with too large a sampling probability to ensure complete traces. - "proportional": Using an OTel-specified consistent sampling mechanism, this sampler reduces the effective sampling probability of each span by `SamplingProbability`.

sampling_percentage.doc: SamplingPercentage is the percentage rate at which traces or logs are going to be sampled. Defaults to zero, i.e.: no sample. Values greater or equal 100 are treated as "sample all traces/logs".

sampling_precision.doc: SamplingPrecision is how many hex digits of sampling threshold will be encoded, from 1 up to 14.  Default is 4. 0 is treated as full precision.

sampling_priority.doc: SamplingPriority (logs only) enables using a log record attribute as the sampling priority of the log record.

fields.doc: Config has the configuration guiding the sampler processor.

allow_all_keys.doc: AllowAllKeys is a flag to allow all span attribute keys. Setting this to true disables the AllowedKeys list. The list of BlockedValues is applied regardless. If you just want to block values, set this to true.

allowed_keys.doc: AllowedKeys is a list of allowed span attribute keys. Span attributes not on the list are removed. The list fails closed if it's empty. To allow all keys, you should explicitly set AllowAllKeys

allowed_values.doc: AllowedValues is a list of regular expressions for allowing values of blocked span attributes. Values that match are not masked.

blocked_key_patterns.doc: BlockedKeyPatterns is a list of blocked span attribute key patterns. Span attributes matching the regexes on the list are masked.

blocked_values.doc: BlockedValues is a list of regular expressions for blocking values of allowed span attributes. Values that match are masked.

attributes.doc: Attributes specifies which attribute keys to apply Elasticsearch sanitization to. If empty, Elasticsearch sanitization is applied to all string values in log bodies but not to span/metric attributes
Attributes specifies which attribute keys to apply Memcached sanitization to. If empty, Memcached sanitization is applied to all string values in log bodies but not to span/metric attributes
Attributes specifies which attribute keys to apply MongoDB sanitization to. If empty, MongoDB sanitization is applied to all string values in log bodies but not to span/metric attributes
Attributes specifies which attribute keys to apply OpenSearch sanitization to. If empty, OpenSearch sanitization is applied to all string values in log bodies but not to span/metric attributes
Attributes specifies which attribute keys to apply Redis sanitization to. If empty, Redis sanitization is applied to all string values in log bodies but not to span/metric attributes
Attributes specifies which attribute keys to apply SQL sanitization to. If empty, SQL sanitization is applied to all string values in log bodies but not to span/metric attributes
Attributes specifies which attribute keys to apply Valkey sanitization to. If empty, Valkey sanitization is applied to all string values in log bodies but not to span/metric attributes

db_sanitizer.doc: DBSanitizer is a flag to enable database query sanitization.

hash_function.doc: HashFunction defines the function for hashing the values instead of masking them with a fixed string. By default, no hash function is used and masking with a fixed string is performed.

hmac_key.doc: HMACKey is the secret key used for HMAC hashing when HashFunction is set to hmac-sha256 or hmac-sha512. This should be loaded from a secure source like environment variables. Minimum length: 32 bytes for HMAC-SHA256, 64 bytes for HMAC-SHA512.

ignored_key_patterns.doc: IgnoredKeyPatterns is a list of attribute key patterns (regex) that are not redacted. attributes matching any of these patterns are allowed to pass through the filter without their values being checked or modified.

ignored_keys.doc: IgnoredKeys is a list of span attribute keys that are not redacted. Span attributes in this list are allowed to pass through the filter without being changed or removed.

redact_all_types.doc: RedactAllTypes of attributes, including those that are not string, by converting to a string representation. By default only string values are redacted.

summary.doc: Summary controls the verbosity level of the diagnostic attributes that the processor adds to the spans when it redacts or masks other attributes. In some contexts a list of redacted attributes leaks information, while it is valuable when integrating and testing a new configuration. Possible values are `debug`, `info`, and `silent`.

attributes.doc: Attributes is the list of attributes that will be sanitized.

sanitize_span_name.doc: SanitizeSpanName controls whether span names should be sanitized.

url_sanitizer.doc: URLSanitization is a flag to sanitize URLs by removing UUIDs, timestamps, and other non-essential information

authenticator.doc: AuthenticatorID specifies the name of the extension to use in order to authenticate the incoming data point.

request_params.doc: RequestParameters is a list of parameters that should be extracted from the request and added to the context. When a parameter is found in both the query string and the header, the value from the query string will be used.

auth.doc: Auth for this receiver

compression_algorithms.doc: CompressionAlgorithms configures the list of compression algorithms the server can accept. Default: ["", "gzip", "zstd", "zlib", "snappy", "deflate"]

allowed_headers.doc: AllowedHeaders sets what headers will be allowed in CORS requests. The Accept, Accept-Language, Content-Type, and Content-Language headers are implicitly allowed. If no headers are listed, X-Requested-With will also be accepted by default. Include "*" to allow any request header.

allowed_origins.doc: AllowedOrigins sets the allowed values of the Origin header for HTTP/JSON requests to an OTLP receiver. An origin may contain a wildcard (*) to replace 0 or more characters (e.g., "http://*.domain.com", or "*" to allow any origin).

max_age.doc: MaxAge sets the value of the Access-Control-Max-Age response header. Set it to the number of seconds that browsers should cache a CORS preflight response for.

cors.doc: CORS configures the server for HTTP cross-origin resource sharing (CORS).

endpoint.doc: Endpoint configures the listening address for the server.

idle_timeout.doc: IdleTimeout is the maximum amount of time to wait for the next request when keep-alives are enabled. If IdleTimeout is zero, the value of ReadTimeout is used. If both are zero, there is no timeout.

include_metadata.doc: IncludeMetadata propagates the client metadata from the incoming requests to the downstream consumers

keep_alives_enabled.doc: KeepAlivesEnabled controls whether HTTP keep-alives are enabled. By default, keep-alives are always enabled. Only very resource-constrained environments should disable them.

limit.doc: Limit is a float that indicates the maximum number of messages repeated through the websocket by this processor in messages per second. Defaults to 1.

max_request_body_size.doc: MaxRequestBodySize sets the maximum request body size in bytes. Default: 20MiB.

id.doc: ID specifies the name of the extension to use.

item.doc: Middleware defines the extension ID for a middleware component.

middlewares.doc: Middlewares are used to add custom functionality to the HTTP server. Middleware handlers are called in the order they appear in this list, with the first middleware becoming the outermost handler.

read_header_timeout.doc: ReadHeaderTimeout is the amount of time allowed to read request headers. The connection's read deadline is reset after reading the headers and the Handler can decide what is considered too slow for the body. If ReadHeaderTimeout is zero, the value of ReadTimeout is used. If both are zero, there is no timeout.

read_timeout.doc: ReadTimeout is the maximum duration for reading the entire request, including the body. A zero or negative value means there will be no timeout. Because ReadTimeout does not let Handlers make per-request decisions on each request body's acceptable deadline or upload rate, most users will prefer to use ReadHeaderTimeout. It is valid to use them both.

write_timeout.doc: WriteTimeout is the maximum duration before timing out writes of the response. It is reset whenever a new request's header is read. Like ReadTimeout, it does not let Handlers make decisions on a per-request basis. A zero or negative value means there will be no timeout.

fields.doc: ServerConfig defines settings for creating an HTTP server.

action.doc: Action specifies the type of action to perform. The set of values are {INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT, DELETE, HASH}. Both lower case and upper case are supported. INSERT -  Inserts the key/value to attributes when the key does not exist. No action is applied to attributes where the key already exists. Either Value, FromAttribute or FromContext must be set. UPDATE -  Updates an existing key with a value. No action is applied to attributes where the key does not exist. Either Value, FromAttribute or FromContext must be set. UPSERT -  Performs insert or update action depending on the attributes containing the key. The key/value is inserted to attributes that did not originally have the key. The key/value is updated for attributes where the key already existed. Either Value, FromAttribute or FromContext must be set. DELETE  - Deletes the attribute. If the key doesn't exist, no action is performed. HASH    - Calculates the SHA-1 hash of an existing value and overwrites the value with its SHA-1 hash result. If the feature gate `coreinternal.attraction.hash.sha256` is enabled, it uses SHA2-256 instead. EXTRACT - Extracts values using a regular expression rule from the input 'key' to target keys specified in the 'rule'. If a target key already exists, it will be overridden. CONVERT  - converts the type of an existing attribute, if convertable This is a required field.

converted_type.doc: ConvertedType specifies the target type of an attribute to be converted If the key doesn't exist, no action is performed. If the value cannot be converted, the original value will be left as-is

default_value.doc: DefaultValue specifies the value to use if Value/FromAttribute/FromContext doesn't provide a value (e.g., environment variable not set, attribute doesn't exist). Only used with INSERT, UPDATE, and UPSERT actions.

from_attribute.doc: FromAttribute specifies the attribute to use to populate the value. If the attribute doesn't exist, no action is performed.

from_context.doc: FromContext specifies the context value to use to populate the value. The values would be searched in client.Info.Metadata. If the key doesn't exist, no action is performed. If the key has multiple values the values will be joined with `;` separator.

key.doc: Key specifies the attribute to act upon. This is a required field.

pattern.doc: A regex pattern must be specified for the action EXTRACT. It uses the attribute specified by `key' to extract values from The target keys are inferred based on the names of the matcher groups provided and the names will be inferred based on the values of the matcher group. Note: All subexpressions must have a name. Note: The value type of the source key must be a string. If it isn't, no extraction will occur.

value.doc: Value specifies the value to populate for the key. The type of the value is inferred from the configuration.

item.doc: ActionKeyValue specifies the attribute key to act upon.

attributes.doc: AttributesActions specifies the list of actions to be applied on resource attributes. The set of actions are {INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT, DELETE, HASH, EXTRACT}.

key.doc: Key specifies the attribute key.

value.doc: Values specifies the value to match against. If it is not set, any value will match.

item.doc: Attribute specifies the attribute key and optional value to match against.

attributes.doc: Attributes specifies the list of attributes to match against. All of these attributes must match for a match to occur. This is an optional field.

version.doc: version match expected actual  match nil      <blank> yes nil      1       yes <blank>  <blank> yes <blank>  1       no 1        <blank> no 1        1       yes

item.doc: InstrumentationLibrary specifies the instrumentation library and optional version to match against.

libraries.doc: Libraries specify the list of items to match the implementation library against. A match occurs if the span's implementation library matches at least one item in this list. This is an optional field.

log_bodies.doc: LogBodies is a list of strings that the LogRecord's body field must match against.

match_undefined.doc: MatchUndefined controls whether logs with "undefined" severity matches. If this is true, entries with undefined severity will match.

min.doc: Min is the lowest severity that may be matched. e.g. if this is plog.SeverityNumberInfo, INFO, WARN, ERROR, and FATAL logs will match.

log_severity_texts.doc: LogSeverityTexts is a list of strings that the LogRecord's severity text field must match against.

match_type.doc: MatchType describes the type of pattern matching a FilterSet uses to filter strings.

metric_names.doc: MetricNames is a list of strings to match metric name against. A match occurs if metric name matches at least one item in the list. This field is optional.

cacheenabled.doc: CacheEnabled determines whether match results are LRU cached to make subsequent matches faster. Cache size is unlimited unless CacheMaxNumEntries is also specified.

cachemaxnumentries.doc: CacheMaxNumEntries is the max number of entries of the LRU cache that stores match results. CacheMaxNumEntries is ignored if CacheEnabled is false.

regexp.doc: Config represents the options for a NewFilterSet.

key.doc: Key specifies the attribute key.

value.doc: Values specifies the value to match against. If it is not set, any value will match.

item.doc: Attribute specifies the attribute key and optional value to match against.

resources.doc: Resources specify the list of items to match the resources against. A match occurs if the data's resources match at least one item in this list. This is an optional field.

services.doc: Services specify the list of items to match service name against. A match occurs if the span's service name matches at least one item in this list. This is an optional field.

span_kinds.doc: SpanKinds specify the list of items to match the span kind against. A match occurs if the span's span kind matches at least one item in this list. This is an optional field

span_names.doc: SpanNames specify the list of items to match span name against. A match occurs if the span name matches at least one item in this list. This is an optional field.

exclude.doc: Exclude specifies when this processor will not be applied to the input data which match the specified properties. Note: The `exclude` properties are checked after the `include` properties, if they exist, are checked. If `include` isn't specified, the `exclude` properties are checked against all input data. This is an optional field. If neither `include` and `exclude` are set, all input data is processed. If `exclude` is set and `include` isn't set, then all the input data that does not match the properties in this structure are processed.

key.doc: Key specifies the attribute key.

value.doc: Values specifies the value to match against. If it is not set, any value will match.

item.doc: Attribute specifies the attribute key and optional value to match against.

attributes.doc: Attributes specifies the list of attributes to match against. All of these attributes must match for a match to occur. This is an optional field.

version.doc: version match expected actual  match nil      <blank> yes nil      1       yes <blank>  <blank> yes <blank>  1       no 1        <blank> no 1        1       yes

item.doc: InstrumentationLibrary specifies the instrumentation library and optional version to match against.

libraries.doc: Libraries specify the list of items to match the implementation library against. A match occurs if the span's implementation library matches at least one item in this list. This is an optional field.

log_bodies.doc: LogBodies is a list of strings that the LogRecord's body field must match against.

match_undefined.doc: MatchUndefined controls whether logs with "undefined" severity matches. If this is true, entries with undefined severity will match.

min.doc: Min is the lowest severity that may be matched. e.g. if this is plog.SeverityNumberInfo, INFO, WARN, ERROR, and FATAL logs will match.

log_severity_number.doc: LogSeverityNumber defines how to match against a log record's SeverityNumber, if defined.

log_severity_texts.doc: LogSeverityTexts is a list of strings that the LogRecord's severity text field must match against.

cachemaxnumentries.doc: CacheMaxNumEntries is the max number of entries of the LRU cache that stores match results. CacheMaxNumEntries is ignored if CacheEnabled is false.

span_names.doc: SpanNames specify the list of items to match span name against. A match occurs if the span name matches at least one item in this list. This is an optional field.

include.doc: Include specifies the set of input data properties that must be present in order for this processor to apply to it. Note: If `exclude` is specified, the input data is compared against those properties after the `include` properties. This is an optional field. If neither `include` and `exclude` are set, all input data are processed. If `include` is set and `exclude` isn't set, then all input data matching the properties in this structure are processed.

from_attributes.doc: FromAttributes represents the attribute keys to pull the values from to generate the new span name. All attribute keys are required in the span to re-name a span. If any attribute is missing from the span, no re-name will occur. Note: The new span name is constructed in order of the `from_attributes` specified in the configuration. This field is required and cannot be empty.

separator.doc: Separator is the string used to separate attributes values in the new span name. If no value is set, no separator is used between attribute values. Used with FromAttributes only.

break_after_match.doc: BreakAfterMatch specifies if processing of rules should stop after the first match. If it is false rule processing will continue to be performed over the modified span name.

keep_original_name.doc: KeepOriginalName specifies if the original span name should be kept after processing the rules. If it is true the original span name will be kept, otherwise it will be replaced with the placeholders of the captured attributes.

rules.doc: Rules is a list of rules to extract attribute values from span name. The values in the span name are replaced by extracted attribute names. Each rule in the list is a regex pattern string. Span name is checked against the regex. If it matches then all named subexpressions of the regex are extracted as attributes and are added to the span. Each subexpression name becomes an attribute name and subexpression matched portion becomes the attribute value. The matched portion in the span name is replaced by extracted attribute name. If the attributes already exist in the span then they will be overwritten. The process is repeated for all rules in the order they are specified. Each subsequent rule works on the span name that is the output after processing the previous rule.

to_attributes.doc: ToAttributes specifies a configuration to extract attributes from span name.

name.doc: Rename specifies the components required to re-name a span. The `from_attributes` field needs to be set for this processor to be properly configured. Note: The field name is `Rename` to avoid collision with the Name() method from config.NamedEntity

code.doc: Code is one of three values "Ok" or "Error" or "Unset". Please check: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/main/specification/trace/api.md#set-status

description.doc: Description is an optional field documenting Error statuses.

status.doc: SetStatus specifies status which should be set for this span.

fields.doc: Config is the configuration for the span processor. Prior to any actions being applied, each span is compared against the include properties and then the exclude properties if they are specified. This determines if a span is to be processed or not.

block_on_overflow.doc: BlockOnOverflow determines the behavior when the component's NumTraces limit is reached. If true, the component will wait for space; otherwise, old traces will be evicted to make space.

non_sampled_cache_size.doc: NonSampledCacheSize specifies the size of the cache that holds the non-sampled trace IDs. This value will be the maximum amount of trace IDs that the cache can hold before overwriting previous IDs. For effective use, this value should be at least an order of magnitude greater than Config.NumTraces. If left as default 0, a no-op DecisionCache will be used.

sampled_cache_size.doc: SampledCacheSize specifies the size of the cache that holds the sampled trace IDs. This value will be the maximum amount of trace IDs that the cache can hold before overwriting previous IDs. For effective use, this value should be at least an order of magnitude greater than Config.NumTraces. If left as default 0, a no-op DecisionCache will be used.

decision_cache.doc: DecisionCache holds configuration for the decision cache(s)

decision_wait.doc: DecisionWait is the time before timer handling for a trace. When sampling_strategy is "trace-complete", this controls decision timing. When sampling_strategy is "span-ingest", this controls pending cleanup finalization timing.

decision_wait_after_root_received.doc: DecisionWaitAfterRootReceived adds root-span-based acceleration for timer handling. When sampling_strategy is "trace-complete", this can make decisions earlier. When sampling_strategy is "span-ingest", this can finalize pending traces earlier on cleanup.

drop_pending_traces_on_shutdown.doc: DropPendingTracesOnShutdown will drop all traces that are part of batches that have not yet reached the decision wait when the processor is shutdown.

expected_new_traces_per_sec.doc: ExpectedNewTracesPerSec sets the expected number of new traces sending to the tail sampling processor per second. This helps with allocating data structures with closer to actual usage size.

maximum_trace_size_bytes.doc: MaximumTraceSizeBytes is the largest size of a trace a decision will be made for. If the trace size exceeds this it will be dropped before the decision period to keep memory more predictable. A 0 value disables dropping large traces early.

num_traces.doc: NumTraces is the number of traces kept on memory. Typically most of the data of a trace is released after a sampling decision is taken.

write_timeout.doc: WriteTimeout is the maximum duration before timing out writes of the response. It is reset whenever a new request's header is read. Like ReadTimeout, it does not let Handlers make decisions on a per-request basis. A zero or negative value means there will be no timeout.

fields.doc: ServerConfig defines settings for creating an HTTP server.

api_version.doc: Docker client API version. If empty, the client will auto-negotiate the API version with the Docker daemon using version negotiation.

collection_interval.doc: CollectionInterval sets how frequently the scraper should be called and used as the context timeout to ensure that scrapers don't exceed the interval.

container_labels_to_metric_labels.doc: A mapping of container label names to MetricDescriptor label keys. The corresponding container label value will become the DataPoint label value for the mapped name.  E.g. `io.kubernetes.container.name: container_spec_name` would result in a MetricDescriptor label called `container_spec_name` whose Metric DataPoints have the value of the `io.kubernetes.container.name` container label.

endpoint.doc: The URL of the docker server. Default is "unix:///var/run/docker.sock" on non-Windows and "npipe:////./pipe/docker_engine" on Windows

env_vars_to_metric_labels.doc: A mapping of container environment variable names to MetricDescriptor label keys.  The corresponding env var values become the DataPoint label value. E.g. `APP_VERSION: version` would result MetricDescriptors having a label key called `version` whose DataPoint label values are the value of the `APP_VERSION` environment variable configured for that particular container, if present.

excluded_images.doc: A list of filters whose matching images are to be excluded. Supports literals, globs, and regex.

initial_delay.doc: InitialDelay sets the initial start delay for the scraper, any non positive value is assumed to be immediately.

stream_stats.doc: StreamStats enables a persistent streaming connection per container to collect stats. When true, each container maintains an open Docker stats stream and the scraper reads from the cached latest value, which reduces connection overhead.  When false (default), a new connection is opened and closed on every scrape cycle, matching the original behavior.

timeout.doc: The maximum amount of time to wait for docker API responses. Default is 5s

ca_file.doc: Path to the CA cert. For a client this verifies the server certificate. For a server this verifies client certificates. If empty uses system root CA. (optional)

cert_file.doc: Path to the TLS cert to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

cert_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS cert to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

cipher_suites.doc: CipherSuites is a list of TLS cipher suites that the TLS transport can use. If left blank, a safe default list is used. See https://go.dev/src/crypto/tls/cipher_suites.go for a list of supported cipher suites.

curve_preferences.doc: contains the elliptic curves that will be used in an ECDHE handshake, in preference order Defaults to empty list and "crypto/tls" defaults are used, internally.

include_system_ca_certs_pool.doc: If true, load system CA certificates pool in addition to the certificates configured in this struct.

insecure.doc: In gRPC and HTTP when set to true, this is used to disable the client transport security. See https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc#WithInsecure for gRPC. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional, default false)

insecure_skip_verify.doc: InsecureSkipVerify will enable TLS but not verify the certificate.

key_file.doc: Path to the TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

key_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

max_version.doc: MaxVersion sets the maximum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, refer to crypto/tls for defaults. (optional)

min_version.doc: MinVersion sets the minimum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, TLS 1.2 will be used. (optional)

reload_interval.doc: ReloadInterval specifies the duration after which the certificate will be reloaded If not set, it will never be reloaded (optional)

server_name_override.doc: ServerName requested by client for virtual hosting. This sets the ServerName in the TLSConfig. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional)

path.doc: The path to the TPM device or Unix domain socket. For instance /dev/tpm0 or /dev/tpmrm0.

tls.doc: TLS holds optional TLS client configuration for connecting to the Docker daemon over HTTPS. When nil (the default), the connection uses no custom TLS — suitable for Unix sockets and plain HTTP endpoints.

fields.doc: ControllerConfig defines common settings for a scraper controller configuration. Scraper controller receivers can embed this struct, instead of receiver.Settings, and extend it with more fields if needed.

authenticator.doc: AuthenticatorID specifies the name of the extension to use in order to authenticate the incoming data point.

auth.doc: Auth configuration for outgoing HTTP calls.

collection_interval.doc: CollectionInterval sets how frequently the scraper should be called and used as the context timeout to ensure that scrapers don't exceed the interval.

compression.doc: The compression key for supported compression types within collector.

compression_params.doc: Advanced configuration options for the Compression

cookies.doc: Cookies configures the cookie management of the HTTP client.

disable_keep_alives.doc: DisableKeepAlives, if true, disables HTTP keep-alives and will only use the connection to the server for a single HTTP request. WARNING: enabling this option can result in significant overhead establishing a new HTTP(S) connection for every request. Before enabling this option please consider whether changes to idle connection settings can achieve your goal.

endpoint.doc: The target URL to send data to (e.g.: http://some.url:9411/v1/traces).

force_attempt_http2.doc: Enabling ForceAttemptHTTP2 forces the HTTP transport to use the HTTP/2 protocol. By default, this is set to true. NOTE: HTTP/2 does not support settings such as MaxConnsPerHost, MaxIdleConnsPerHost and MaxIdleConns.

value.doc: String alias that is marshaled and printed in an opaque way. To recover the original value, cast it to a string.

item.doc: Pair is an element of a MapList, and consists of a name and an opaque value.

headers.doc: Additional headers attached to each HTTP request sent by the client. Existing header values are overwritten if collision happens. Header values are opaque since they may be sensitive.

http2_ping_timeout.doc: HTTP2PingTimeout if there's no response to the ping within the configured value, the connection will be closed. If not set or set to 0, it defaults to 15s.

http2_read_idle_timeout.doc: This is needed in case you run into https://github.com/golang/go/issues/59690 https://github.com/golang/go/issues/36026 HTTP2ReadIdleTimeout if the connection has been idle for the configured value send a ping frame for health check 0s means no health check will be performed.

idle_conn_timeout.doc: IdleConnTimeout is the maximum amount of time a connection will remain open before closing itself. By default, it is set to 90 seconds.

indices.doc: Indices defines the indices to scrape. See https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/indices-stats.html#index-stats-api-path-params for which names are viable. If Indices is empty, no indices will be scraped.

initial_delay.doc: InitialDelay sets the initial start delay for the scraper, any non positive value is assumed to be immediately.

max_conns_per_host.doc: MaxConnsPerHost limits the total number of connections per host, including connections in the dialing, active, and idle states. Default is 0 (unlimited).

max_idle_conns.doc: MaxIdleConns is used to set a limit to the maximum idle HTTP connections the client can keep open. By default, it is set to 100. Zero means no limit.

max_idle_conns_per_host.doc: MaxIdleConnsPerHost is used to set a limit to the maximum idle HTTP connections the host can keep open. If zero, [net/http.DefaultMaxIdleConnsPerHost] is used.

max_idle_conns.doc: MaxIdleConns is used to set a limit to the maximum idle HTTP connections the client can keep open. By default, it is set to 100. Zero means no limit.

max_idle_conns_per_host.doc: MaxIdleConnsPerHost is used to set a limit to the maximum idle HTTP connections the host can keep open. If zero, [net/http.DefaultMaxIdleConnsPerHost] is used.

Because ReadTimeout does not let Handlers make per-request decisions on each request body's acceptable deadline or upload rate, most users will prefer to use ReadHeaderTimeout. max_interval.doc: MaxInterval is the upper bound on backoff interval. Once this value is reached the delay between consecutive retries will always be `MaxInterval`. Default value is 30 seconds.

retry_on_failure.doc: Config defines configuration for retrying batches in case of receiving a retryable error from a downstream consumer. If the retryable error doesn't provide a delay, exponential backoff is applied.

fields.doc: Config defines configuration for kubernetes cluster receiver.

auth_type.doc: How to authenticate to the K8s API server.  This can be one of `none` (for no auth), `serviceAccount` (to use the standard service account token provided to the agent pod), or `kubeConfig` to use credentials from `~/.kube/config`.

context.doc: When using auth_type `kubeConfig`, override the current context.

kube_api_burst.doc: KubeAPIBurst is the maximum burst of requests to the Kubernetes API. Uses client-go's default (10) if unset. Increase if you see client-side throttling warnings.

kube_api_qps.doc: KubeAPIQPS is the maximum number of queries per second to the Kubernetes API. Uses client-go's default (5) if unset. Increase if you see client-side throttling warnings.

namespaces.doc: List of ‘namespaces’ to collect events from.

fields.doc: Config defines configuration for kubernetes events receiver.

auth_type.doc: How to authenticate to the K8s API server.  This can be one of `none` (for no auth), `serviceAccount` (to use the standard service account token provided to the agent pod), or `kubeConfig` to use credentials from `~/.kube/config`.

context.doc: When using auth_type `kubeConfig`, override the current context.

kube_api_burst.doc: KubeAPIBurst is the maximum burst of requests to the Kubernetes API. Uses client-go's default (10) if unset. Increase if you see client-side throttling warnings.

kube_api_qps.doc: KubeAPIQPS is the maximum number of queries per second to the Kubernetes API. Uses client-go's default (5) if unset. Increase if you see client-side throttling warnings.

item.doc: Config configures the matching behavior of a Filter.

fields.doc: APIConfig contains options relevant to connecting to the K8s API

plain_text.doc: PlainText is an alias for SASL/PLAIN authentication. Deprecated [v0.123.0]: use SASL with Mechanism set to PLAIN instead.

region.doc: Region is the AWS region the MSK cluster is based in

aws_msk.doc: AWSMSK holds configuration specific to AWS MSK.

mechanism.doc: SASL Mechanism to be used, possible values are: (PLAIN, AWS_MSK_IAM_OAUTHBEARER, OAUTHBEARER, SCRAM-SHA-256 or SCRAM-SHA-512).

oauthbearer_token_source.doc: ID of type "extension" providing a TokenSource for OAUTHBEARER Mechanism, typically named "oauth2client"

password.doc: Password to be used on authentication

username.doc: Username to be used on authentication

version.doc: SASL Protocol Version to be used, possible values are: (0, 1). Defaults to 0.

ca_file.doc: Path to the CA cert. For a client this verifies the server certificate. For a server this verifies client certificates. If empty uses system root CA. (optional)

cert_file.doc: Path to the TLS cert to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

cert_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS cert to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

cipher_suites.doc: CipherSuites is a list of TLS cipher suites that the TLS transport can use. If left blank, a safe default list is used. See https://go.dev/src/crypto/tls/cipher_suites.go for a list of supported cipher suites.

curve_preferences.doc: contains the elliptic curves that will be used in an ECDHE handshake, in preference order Defaults to empty list and "crypto/tls" defaults are used, internally.

include_system_ca_certs_pool.doc: If true, load system CA certificates pool in addition to the certificates configured in this struct.

insecure.doc: In gRPC and HTTP when set to true, this is used to disable the client transport security. See https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc#WithInsecure for gRPC. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional, default false)

insecure_skip_verify.doc: InsecureSkipVerify will enable TLS but not verify the certificate.

key_file.doc: Path to the TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

key_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

max_version.doc: MaxVersion sets the maximum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, refer to crypto/tls for defaults. (optional)

min_version.doc: MinVersion sets the minimum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, TLS 1.2 will be used. (optional)

reload_interval.doc: ReloadInterval specifies the duration after which the certificate will be reloaded If not set, it will never be reloaded (optional)

server_name_override.doc: ServerName requested by client for virtual hosting. This sets the ServerName in the TLSConfig. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional)

path.doc: The path to the TPM device or Unix domain socket. For instance /dev/tpm0 or /dev/tpmrm0.

tls.doc: TLS holds TLS configuration for connecting to Kafka brokers. Deprecated [v0.124.0]: use ClientConfig.TLS instead. This will be used only if ClientConfig.TLS is not set.

auth.doc: Authentication holds Kafka authentication details.

enable.doc: Whether or not to auto-commit updated offsets back to the broker. (default enabled).

interval.doc: How frequently to commit updated offsets. Ineffective unless auto-commit is enabled (default 1s)

autocommit.doc: AutoCommit controls the auto-commit functionality of the consumer.

brokers.doc: Brokers holds the list of Kafka bootstrap servers (default localhost:9092).

client_id.doc: ClientID holds the client ID advertised to Kafka, which can be used for enforcing ACLs, throttling quotas, and more (default "otel-collector")

conn_idle_timeout.doc: ConnIdleTimeout specifies the time after which idle connections are not reused and may be closed.

enabled.doc: Enabled indicates whether to not retry sending batches in case of export failure.

initial_interval.doc: InitialInterval the time to wait after the first failure before retrying.

max_elapsed_time.doc: MaxElapsedTime is the maximum amount of time (including retries) spent trying to send a request/batch. Once this value is reached, the data is discarded. If set to 0, the retries are never stopped.

max_interval.doc: MaxInterval is the upper bound on backoff interval. Once this value is reached the delay between consecutive retries will always be `MaxInterval`.

multiplier.doc: Multiplier is the value multiplied by the backoff interval bounds

randomization_factor.doc: RandomizationFactor is a random factor used to calculate next backoffs Randomized interval = RetryInterval * (1 ± RandomizationFactor)

error_backoff.doc: ErrorBackoff controls backoff/retry behavior when the next consumer returns an error.

group_id.doc: GroupID specifies the ID of the consumer group that will be consuming messages from (default "otel-collector").

group_instance_id.doc: GroupInstanceID specifies the ID of the consumer

group_rebalance_strategy.doc: GroupRebalanceStrategy specifies the strategy to use for partition assignment. Possible values are "range", "roundrobin", "sticky", and "cooperative-sticky". Defaults to "cooperative-sticky"

header_extraction.doc: HeaderExtraction controls extraction of headers from Kafka records.

heartbeat_interval.doc: HeartbeatInterval controls the Kafka consumer group coordination heartbeat interval. Heartbeats ensure the consumer's session remains active.

initial_offset.doc: InitialOffset specifies the initial offset to use if no offset was previously committed. Must be `latest` or `earliest` (default "latest").

encoding.doc: Encoding holds the expected encoding of messages for the signal type Defaults to "otlp_proto".

exclude_topics.doc: Optional exclude topics option, used only in regex mode.

topics.doc: Topics holds the name of the Kafka topics from which messages of the signal type should be consumed. The default depends on the signal type: - "otlp_spans" for traces - "otlp_metrics" for metrics - "otlp_logs" for logs - "otlp_profiles" for profiles

logs.doc: Logs holds configuration about how logs should be consumed.

max_fetch_size.doc: The maximum bytes per fetch from Kafka (default "1048576")

max_fetch_wait.doc: The maximum amount of time to wait for MinFetchSize bytes to be available before the broker returns a response (default 250ms)

max_partition_fetch_size.doc: MaxPartitionFetchSize defines the maximum number of bytes to fetch per partition (default "1048576")

after.doc: If true, the messages are marked after the pipeline execution

on_error.doc: If false, only the successfully processed messages are marked. This only applies to non-permanent errors. It has no impact if After is set to false. Note: this can block the entire partition in case a message processing returns a non-permanent error.

on_permanent_error.doc: If false, only the successfully processed messages are marked. This only applies to permanent errors. It has no impact if After is set to false. message_marking.doc: MessageMarking controls the way the messages are marked as consumed.

read_header_timeout.doc: ReadHeaderTimeout is the amount of time allowed to read request headers. The connection's read deadline is reset after reading the headers and the Handler can decide what is considered too slow for the body. If ReadHeaderTimeout is zero, the value of ReadTimeout is used. If both are zero, there is no timeout.

read_timeout.doc: ReadTimeout is the maximum duration for reading the entire request, including the body. A zero or negative value means there will be no timeout. Because ReadTimeout does not let Handlers make per-request decisions on each request body's acceptable deadline or upload rate, most users will prefer to use ReadHeaderTimeout. It is valid to use them both.

enabled.doc: Enabled indicates whether to not retry sending batches in case of export failure.

initial_interval.doc: InitialInterval the time to wait after the first failure before retrying.

max_elapsed_time.doc: MaxElapsedTime is the maximum amount of time (including retries) spent trying to send a request/batch. Once this value is reached, the data is discarded. If set to 0, the retries are never stopped.

max_interval.doc: MaxInterval is the upper bound on backoff interval. Once this value is reached the delay between consecutive retries will always be `MaxInterval`.

multiplier.doc: Multiplier is the value multiplied by the backoff interval bounds

randomization_factor.doc: RandomizationFactor is a random factor used to calculate next backoffs Randomized interval = RetryInterval * (1 ± RandomizationFactor)

retry_on_failure.doc: BackOffConfig defines configuration for retrying batches in case of export failure. The current supported strategy is exponential backoff.

secret.doc: String alias that is marshaled and printed in an opaque way. To recover the original value, cast it to a string.

ca_file.doc: Path to the CA cert. For a client this verifies the server certificate. For a server this verifies client certificates. If empty uses system root CA. (optional)

cert_file.doc: Path to the TLS cert to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

cert_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS cert to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

cipher_suites.doc: CipherSuites is a list of TLS cipher suites that the TLS transport can use. If left blank, a safe default list is used. See https://go.dev/src/crypto/tls/cipher_suites.go for a list of supported cipher suites.

client_ca_file.doc: Path to the TLS cert to use by the server to verify a client certificate. (optional) This sets the ClientCAs and ClientAuth to RequireAndVerifyClientCert in the TLSConfig. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional)

client_ca_file_reload.doc: Reload the ClientCAs file when it is modified (optional, default false)

curve_preferences.doc: contains the elliptic curves that will be used in an ECDHE handshake, in preference order Defaults to empty list and "crypto/tls" defaults are used, internally.

include_system_ca_certs_pool.doc: If true, load system CA certificates pool in addition to the certificates configured in this struct.

key_file.doc: Path to the TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

key_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

max_version.doc: MaxVersion sets the maximum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, refer to crypto/tls for defaults. (optional)

min_version.doc: MinVersion sets the minimum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, TLS 1.2 will be used. (optional)

reload_interval.doc: ReloadInterval specifies the duration after which the certificate will be reloaded If not set, it will never be reloaded (optional)

path.doc: The path to the TPM device or Unix domain socket. For instance /dev/tpm0 or /dev/tpmrm0.

tls.doc: ServerConfig contains TLS configurations that are specific to server connections in addition to the common configurations. This should be used by components configuring TLS server connections.

collection_interval.doc: CollectionInterval sets how frequently the scraper should be called and used as the context timeout to ensure that scrapers don't exceed the interval.

events.doc: EventsConfig is the configuration options for events collection

initial_delay.doc: InitialDelay sets the initial start delay for the scraper, any non positive value is assumed to be immediately.

endpoint.doc: Endpoint configures the address for this network connection. For TCP and UDP networks, the address has the form "host:port". enabled.doc: Enabled indicates whether to not retry sending logs in case of receiving a retryable error from a downstream consumer. Default is false.

initial_interval.doc: InitialInterval the time to wait after the first failure before retrying. Default value is 1 second.

max_elapsed_time.doc: MaxElapsedTime is the maximum amount of time (including retries) spent trying to send a logs batch to a downstream consumer. Once this value is reached, the data is discarded. It never stops if MaxElapsedTime == 0. Default value is 5 minutes.

max_interval.doc: MaxInterval is the upper bound on backoff interval. Once this value is reached the delay between consecutive retries will always be `MaxInterval`. Default value is 30 seconds.

retry_on_failure.doc: Config defines configuration for retrying batches in case of receiving a retryable error from a downstream consumer. If the retryable error doesn't provide a delay, exponential backoff is applied.

request_limit_mib.doc: RequestLimitMiB limits the number of requests that are received by the stream based on uncompressed request size. Request size is used to control how much traffic we admit for processing.  When this field is zero, admission control is disabled.

waiting_limit_mib.doc: WaitingLimitMiB is the limit on the amount of data waiting to be consumed. This is a dimension of memory limiting to ensure waiters are not consuming an unexpectedly large amount of memory in the arrow receiver.

admission.doc: Admission is the configuration for controlling amount of request memory entering the receiver.

admission_limit_mib.doc: Deprecated: This field is no longer supported, use cfg.Admission.RequestLimitMiB instead.

memory_limit_mib.doc: MemoryLimitMiB is the size of a shared memory region used by all Arrow streams, in MiB.  When too much load is passing through, they will see ResourceExhausted errors.

waiter_limit.doc: Deprecated: This field is no longer supported, use cfg.Admission.WaiterLimit instead.

concurrency.doc: Concurrency is a Zstd-library parameter that configures the use of background goroutines to improve decompression speed. 0 means to let the library decide (it will use up to GOMAXPROCS), and 1 means to avoid background workers.  (default: 1) See `zstdlib.WithDecoderConcurrency()`.

max_window_size_mib.doc: MaxWindowSizeMiB limits window sizes that can be configured in the corresponding encoder's `EncoderConfig.WindowSizeMiB` setting, as a way to control memory usage. See `zstdlib.WithDecoderMaxWindow()`.

memory_limit_mib.doc: MemoryLimitMiB is a memory limit control for the decoder, as a way to limit overall memory use by Zstd. See `zstdlib.WithDecoderMaxMemory()`.

dialer.doc: DialerConfig contains options for connecting to an address.

endpoint.doc: Endpoint configures the address for this network connection. For TCP and UDP networks, the address has the form "host:port". The host must be a literal IP address, or a host name that can be resolved to IP addresses. The port must be a literal port number or a service name. If the host is a literal IPv6 address it must be enclosed in square brackets, as in "[2001:db8::1]:80" or "[fe80::1%zone]:80". The zone specifies the scope of the literal IPv6 address as defined in RFC 4007.

include_metadata.doc: Include propagates the incoming connection's metadata to downstream consumers.

enforcement_policy.doc: KeepaliveEnforcementPolicy allow configuration of the keepalive.EnforcementPolicy. The same default values as keepalive.EnforcementPolicy are applicable and get applied by the server. See https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc/keepalive#EnforcementPolicy for details.

server_parameters.doc: KeepaliveServerParameters allow configuration of the keepalive.ServerParameters. The same default values as keepalive.ServerParameters are applicable and get applied by the server. See https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc/keepalive#ServerParameters for details.

keepalive.doc: Keepalive anchor for all the settings related to keepalive.

max_concurrent_streams.doc: MaxConcurrentStreams sets the limit on the number of concurrent streams to each ServerTransport. It has effect only for streaming RPCs.

max_recv_msg_size_mib.doc: MaxRecvMsgSizeMiB sets the maximum size (in MiB) of messages accepted by the server.

block_profile_fraction.doc: Self-scraper only: Fraction of blocking events that are profiled. A value <= 0 disables profiling. See https://golang.org/pkg/runtime/#SetBlockProfileRate for details.

collection_interval.doc: CollectionInterval sets how frequently the scraper should be called and used as the context timeout to ensure that scrapers don't exceed the interval.

compression.doc: The compression key for supported compression types within collector.

compression_params.doc: Advanced configuration options for the Compression

cookies.doc: Cookies configures the cookie management of the HTTP client.

disable_keep_alives.doc: DisableKeepAlives, if true, disables HTTP keep-alives and will only use the connection to the server for a single HTTP request. WARNING: enabling this option can result in significant overhead establishing a new HTTP(S) connection for every request. Before enabling this option please consider whether changes to idle connection settings can achieve your goal.

endpoint.doc: The target URL to send data to (e.g.: http://some.url:9411/v1/traces).

force_attempt_http2.doc: Enabling ForceAttemptHTTP2 forces the HTTP transport to use the HTTP/2 protocol. By default, this is set to true. NOTE: HTTP/2 does not support settings such as MaxConnsPerHost, MaxIdleConnsPerHost and MaxIdleConns.

value.doc: String alias that is marshaled and printed in an opaque way. To recover the original value, cast it to a string.

item.doc: Pair is an element of a MapList, and consists of a name and an opaque value.

headers.doc: Additional headers attached to each HTTP request sent by the client. Existing header values are overwritten if collision happens. Header values are opaque since they may be sensitive.

http2_ping_timeout.doc: HTTP2PingTimeout if there's no response to the ping within the configured value, the connection will be closed. If not set or set to 0, it defaults to 15s.

http2_read_idle_timeout.doc: This is needed in case you run into https://github.com/golang/go/issues/59690 https://github.com/golang/go/issues/36026 HTTP2ReadIdleTimeout if the connection has been idle for the configured value send a ping frame for health check 0s means no health check will be performed.

idle_conn_timeout.doc: IdleConnTimeout is the maximum amount of time a connection will remain open before closing itself. By default, it is set to 90 seconds.

include.doc: Include is the glob pattern for pprof files to scrape.

initial_delay.doc: InitialDelay sets the initial start delay for the scraper, any non positive value is assumed to be immediately.

max_conns_per_host.doc: MaxConnsPerHost limits the total number of connections per host, including connections in the dialing, active, and idle states. Default is 0 (unlimited).

max_idle_conns.doc: MaxIdleConns is used to set a limit to the maximum idle HTTP connections the client can keep open. By default, it is set to 100. Zero means no limit.

headers.doc: Additional headers attached to each HTTP request sent by the client. Existing header values are overwritten if collision happens. Header values are opaque since they may be sensitive.

http2_ping_timeout.doc: HTTP2PingTimeout if there's no response to the ping within the configured value, the connection will be closed. If not set or set to 0, it defaults to 15s.

http2_read_idle_timeout.doc: This is needed in case you run into https://github.com/golang/go/issues/59690 https://github.com/golang/go/issues/36026 HTTP2ReadIdleTimeout if the connection has been idle for the configured value send a ping frame for health check 0s means no health check will be performed.

idle_conn_timeout.doc: IdleConnTimeout is the maximum amount of time a connection will remain open before closing itself. By default, it is set to 90 seconds.

max_conns_per_host.doc: MaxConnsPerHost limits the total number of connections per host, including connections in the dialing, active, and idle states. Default is 0 (unlimited).

max_idle_conns.doc: MaxIdleConns is used to set a limit to the maximum idle HTTP connections the client can keep open. By default, it is set to 100. Zero means no limit.

max_idle_conns_per_host.doc: MaxIdleConnsPerHost is used to set a limit to the maximum idle HTTP connections the host can keep open. If zero, [net/http.DefaultMaxIdleConnsPerHost] is used.

middlewares.doc: Middlewares are used to add custom functionality to the HTTP client. Middleware handlers are called in the order they appear in this list, with the first middleware becoming the outermost handler.

read_buffer_size.doc: ReadBufferSize for HTTP client. See http.Transport.ReadBufferSize. Default is 0.

timeout.doc: Timeout parameter configures `http.Client.Timeout`. Default is 0 (unlimited).

curve_preferences.doc: contains the elliptic curves that will be used in an ECDHE handshake, in preference order Defaults to empty list and "crypto/tls" defaults are used, internally.

include_system_ca_certs_pool.doc: If true, load system CA certificates pool in addition to the certificates configured in this struct.

insecure.doc: In gRPC and HTTP when set to true, this is used to disable the client transport security. See https://godoc.org/google.golang.org/grpc#WithInsecure for gRPC. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional, default false)

insecure_skip_verify.doc: InsecureSkipVerify will enable TLS but not verify the certificate.

key_file.doc: Path to the TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

max_version.doc: MaxVersion sets the maximum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, refer to crypto/tls for defaults. (optional)

reload_interval.doc: ReloadInterval specifies the duration after which the certificate will be reloaded If not set, it will never be reloaded (optional)

server_name_override.doc: ServerName requested by client for virtual hosting. This sets the ServerName in the TLSConfig. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional)

timeout.doc: Timeout is the maximum amount of time a dial will wait for a connect to complete. The default is no timeout.

dialer.doc: DialerConfig contains options for connecting to an address.

endpoint.doc: Endpoint configures the address for this network connection. The address has the form "host:port". The host must be a literal IP address, or a host name that can be resolved to IP addresses. The port must be a literal port number or a service name. If the host is a literal IPv6 address it must be enclosed in square brackets, as in "[2001:db8::1]:80" or "[fe80::1%zone]:80". The zone specifies the scope of the literal IPv6 address as defined in RFC 4007.

extract_collectd_tags.doc: ExtractCollectdTags instructs the Wavefront receiver to attempt to extract tags in the CollectD format from the metric name. The default is false.

tcp_idle_timeout.doc: TCPIdleTimeout is the timeout for idle TCP connections.

request_params.doc: RequestParameters is a list of parameters that should be extracted from the request and added to the context. When a parameter is found in both the query string and the header, the value from the query string will be used.

auth.doc: Auth for this receiver

compression_algorithms.doc: CompressionAlgorithms configures the list of compression algorithms the server can accept. Default: ["", "gzip", "zstd", "zlib", "snappy", "deflate"]

allowed_headers.doc: AllowedHeaders sets what headers will be allowed in CORS requests. The Accept, Accept-Language, Content-Type, and Content-Language headers are implicitly allowed. If no headers are listed, X-Requested-With will also be accepted by default. Include "*" to allow any request header.

allowed_origins.doc: AllowedOrigins sets the allowed values of the Origin header for HTTP/JSON requests to an OTLP receiver. An origin may contain a wildcard (*) to replace 0 or more characters (e.g., "http://*.domain.com", or "*" to allow any origin).

max_age.doc: MaxAge sets the value of the Access-Control-Max-Age response header. Set it to the number of seconds that browsers should cache a CORS preflight response for.

cors.doc: CORS configures the server for HTTP cross-origin resource sharing (CORS).

endpoint.doc: Endpoint configures the listening address for the server.

idle_timeout.doc: IdleTimeout is the maximum amount of time to wait for the next request when keep-alives are enabled. If IdleTimeout is zero, the value of ReadTimeout is used. If both are zero, there is no timeout.

include_metadata.doc: IncludeMetadata propagates the client metadata from the incoming requests to the downstream consumers

keep_alives_enabled.doc: KeepAlivesEnabled controls whether HTTP keep-alives are enabled. By default, keep-alives are always enabled. Only very resource-constrained environments should disable them.

max_request_body_size.doc: MaxRequestBodySize sets the maximum request body size in bytes. Default: 20MiB.

id.doc: ID specifies the name of the extension to use.

item.doc: Middleware defines the extension ID for a middleware component.

middlewares.doc: Middlewares are used to add custom functionality to the HTTP server. Middleware handlers are called in the order they appear in this list, with the first middleware becoming the outermost handler.

read_header_timeout.doc: ReadHeaderTimeout is the amount of time allowed to read request headers. The connection's read deadline is reset after reading the headers and the Handler can decide what is considered too slow for the body. If ReadHeaderTimeout is zero, the value of ReadTimeout is used. If both are zero, there is no timeout.

value.doc: String alias that is marshaled and printed in an opaque way. To recover the original value, cast it to a string.

item.doc: Pair is an element of a MapList, and consists of a name and an opaque value.

response_headers.doc: Additional headers attached to each HTTP response sent to the client. Header values are opaque since they may be sensitive.

cert_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS cert to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

client_ca_file_reload.doc: Reload the ClientCAs file when it is modified (optional, default false)

curve_preferences.doc: contains the elliptic curves that will be used in an ECDHE handshake, in preference order Defaults to empty list and "crypto/tls" defaults are used, internally.

include_system_ca_certs_pool.doc: If true, load system CA certificates pool in addition to the certificates configured in this struct.

key_file.doc: Path to the TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

key_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

max_version.doc: MaxVersion sets the maximum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, refer to crypto/tls for defaults. (optional)

min_version.doc: MinVersion sets the minimum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, TLS 1.2 will be used. (optional)

reload_interval.doc: ReloadInterval specifies the duration after which the certificate will be reloaded If not set, it will never be reloaded (optional)

max_interval.doc: MaxInterval is the upper bound on backoff interval. Once this value is reached the delay between consecutive retries will always be `MaxInterval`. Default value is 30 seconds.

idle_timeout.doc: IdleTimeout is the maximum amount of time to wait for the next request when keep-alives are enabled. If IdleTimeout is zero, the value of ReadTimeout is used. If both are zero, there is no timeout.

include_metadata.doc: IncludeMetadata propagates the client metadata from the incoming requests to the downstream consumers

keep_alives_enabled.doc: KeepAlivesEnabled controls whether HTTP keep-alives are enabled. By default, keep-alives are always enabled. Only very resource-constrained environments should disable them.

max_request_body_size.doc: MaxRequestBodySize sets the maximum request body size in bytes. Default: 20MiB.

id.doc: ID specifies the name of the extension to use.

item.doc: Middleware defines the extension ID for a middleware component.

middlewares.doc: Middlewares are used to add custom functionality to the HTTP server. Middleware handlers are called in the order they appear in this list, with the first middleware becoming the outermost handler.

parse_string_tags.doc: If enabled the zipkin receiver will attempt to parse string tags/binary annotations into int/bool/float. Disabled by default

read_header_timeout.doc: ReadHeaderTimeout is the amount of time allowed to read request headers. The connection's read deadline is reset after reading the headers and the Handler can decide what is considered too slow for the body. If ReadHeaderTimeout is zero, the value of ReadTimeout is used. If both are zero, there is no timeout.

read_timeout.doc: ReadTimeout is the maximum duration for reading the entire request, including the body. A zero or negative value means there will be no timeout. Because ReadTimeout does not let Handlers make per-request decisions on each request body's acceptable deadline or upload rate, most users will prefer to use ReadHeaderTimeout. It is valid to use them both.

value.doc: String alias that is marshaled and printed in an opaque way. To recover the original value, cast it to a string.

item.doc: Pair is an element of a MapList, and consists of a name and an opaque value.

response_headers.doc: Additional headers attached to each HTTP response sent to the client. Header values are opaque since they may be sensitive.

ca_file.doc: Path to the CA cert. For a client this verifies the server certificate. For a server this verifies client certificates. If empty uses system root CA. (optional)

cert_file.doc: Path to the TLS cert to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

cert_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS cert to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

cipher_suites.doc: CipherSuites is a list of TLS cipher suites that the TLS transport can use. If left blank, a safe default list is used. See https://go.dev/src/crypto/tls/cipher_suites.go for a list of supported cipher suites.

client_ca_file.doc: Path to the TLS cert to use by the server to verify a client certificate. (optional) This sets the ClientCAs and ClientAuth to RequireAndVerifyClientCert in the TLSConfig. Please refer to https://godoc.org/crypto/tls#Config for more information. (optional)

client_ca_file_reload.doc: Reload the ClientCAs file when it is modified (optional, default false)

curve_preferences.doc: contains the elliptic curves that will be used in an ECDHE handshake, in preference order Defaults to empty list and "crypto/tls" defaults are used, internally.

include_system_ca_certs_pool.doc: If true, load system CA certificates pool in addition to the certificates configured in this struct.

key_file.doc: Path to the TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

key_pem.doc: In memory PEM encoded TLS key to use for TLS required connections. (optional)

max_version.doc: MaxVersion sets the maximum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, refer to crypto/tls for defaults. (optional)

min_version.doc: MinVersion sets the minimum TLS version that is acceptable. If not set, TLS 1.2 will be used. (optional)

reload_interval.doc: ReloadInterval specifies the duration after which the certificate will be reloaded If not set, it will never be reloaded (optional)

path.doc: The path to the TPM device or Unix domain socket. For instance /dev/tpm0 or /dev/tpmrm0.

tls.doc: TLS struct exposes TLS client configuration.

write_timeout.doc: WriteTimeout is the maximum duration before timing out writes of the response. It is reset whenever a new request's header is read. Like ReadTimeout, it does not let Handlers make decisions on a per-request basis. A zero or negative value means there will be no timeout.

fields.doc: Config defines configuration for Zipkin receiver.

collection_interval.doc: CollectionInterval sets how frequently the scraper should be called and used as the context timeout to ensure that scrapers don't exceed the interval.

timeout.doc: Timeout is the maximum amount of time a dial will wait for a connect to complete. The default is no timeout.

dialer.doc: DialerConfig contains options for connecting to an address.

endpoint.doc: Endpoint configures the address for this network connection. The address has the form "host:port". The host must be a literal IP address, or a host name that can be resolved to IP addresses. The port must be a literal port number or a service name. If the host is a literal IPv6 address it must be enclosed in square brackets, as in "[2001:db8::1]:80" or "[fe80::1%zone]:80". The zone specifies the scope of the literal IPv6 address as defined in RFC 4007.

initial_delay.doc: InitialDelay sets the initial start delay for the scraper, any non positive value is assumed to be immediately.

zookeeper.connection.active.doc: ZookeeperConnectionActiveMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.connection.active metric.

zookeeper.data_tree.ephemeral_node.count.doc: ZookeeperDataTreeEphemeralNodeCountMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.data_tree.ephemeral_node.count metric.

zookeeper.data_tree.size.doc: ZookeeperDataTreeSizeMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.data_tree.size metric.

zookeeper.file_descriptor.limit.doc: ZookeeperFileDescriptorLimitMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.file_descriptor.limit metric.

zookeeper.file_descriptor.open.doc: ZookeeperFileDescriptorOpenMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.file_descriptor.open metric.

zookeeper.follower.count.doc: ZookeeperFollowerCountMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.follower.count metric.

zookeeper.fsync.exceeded_threshold.count.doc: ZookeeperFsyncExceededThresholdCountMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.fsync.exceeded_threshold.count metric.

zookeeper.latency.avg.doc: ZookeeperLatencyAvgMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.latency.avg metric.

zookeeper.latency.max.doc: ZookeeperLatencyMaxMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.latency.max metric.

zookeeper.latency.min.doc: ZookeeperLatencyMinMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.latency.min metric.

zookeeper.packet.count.doc: ZookeeperPacketCountMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.packet.count metric.

zookeeper.request.active.doc: ZookeeperRequestActiveMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.request.active metric.

zookeeper.ruok.doc: ZookeeperRuokMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.ruok metric.

zookeeper.sync.pending.doc: ZookeeperSyncPendingMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.sync.pending metric.

zookeeper.watch.count.doc: ZookeeperWatchCountMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.watch.count metric.

zookeeper.znode.count.doc: ZookeeperZnodeCountMetricConfig provides config for the zookeeper.znode.count metric.

metrics.doc: MetricsConfig provides config for zookeeper metrics.

item.doc: Config configures the matching behavior of a Filter.

metrics_exclude.doc: Experimental: MetricsExclude defines a list of filters for attribute values. If the list is not empty, metrics with matching resource attribute values will not be emitted. MetricsInclude has higher priority than MetricsExclude.

item.doc: Config configures the matching behavior of a Filter.

metrics_include.doc: Experimental: MetricsInclude defines a list of filters for attribute values. If the list is not empty, only metrics with matching resource attribute values will be emitted.

server.state.doc: ResourceAttributeConfig provides common config for a server.state resource attribute.

item.doc: Config configures the matching behavior of a Filter.

metrics_exclude.doc: Experimental: MetricsExclude defines a list of filters for attribute values. If the list is not empty, metrics with matching resource attribute values will not be emitted. MetricsInclude has higher priority than MetricsExclude.

item.doc: Config configures the matching behavior of a Filter.

metrics_include.doc: Experimental: MetricsInclude defines a list of filters for attribute values. If the list is not empty, only metrics with matching resource attribute values will be emitted.

zk.version.doc: ResourceAttributeConfig provides common config for a zk.version resource attribute.

resource_attributes.doc: ResourceAttributesConfig provides config for zookeeper resource attributes.

timeout.doc: Timeout is an optional value used to set scraper's context deadline.

fields.doc: ControllerConfig defines common settings for a scraper controller configuration. Scraper controller receivers can embed this struct, instead of receiver.Settings, and extend it with more fields if needed.
